reviews.author: Paul Elliott
reviews.text: There are very few films that are as prudent and as sustainedly controlled in their storytelling as Raoul Walsh’s White Heat. Starring James Cagney in a powerhouse performance as Arthur "Cody" Jarrett, it delivers a volatile completion to Warner Brother's rotation of gangster movies which started in 1931 with Little Caesar. It abides as possibly the pinnacle performance in Cagney’s lengthy and diverse career, as well as being the movie that contains the frequently misquoted "Made it, Ma! Top of the world!". It’s all riveted together beautifully by Walsh's vehement and polished direction and unhesitatingly stands as one of the most pre-eminent of all gangster epics.

reviews.text: First of all, I need to remember that William A. Wellman was not just any director; his biography is irredeemably intertwined with the story he set out to tell. A veteran of the First World War and one of the few American filmmakers to have served as a combat pilot in the French Foreign Legion, Wellman brings to the film a surreal authenticity, especially in the aerial sequences. The camera is incredibly innovative for its time, capturing with astonishing vigor the acrobatics of biplane aircraft and the chaos of battle. The film is truly a technical phenomenon that anticipates by decades the grandiloquence of Hollywood war blockbusters.

reviews.text: Woodstock takes a little while to get you hooked and to reveal its tremendous impact. Your initial impression may be that it is more an experience than a film and basically requiring an all-day commitment to watch, that may be accurate. But it is also a must-see achievement in film, capturing with no shortage of style or substance something bigger than music: a cultural event that defined a generation. Full review HERE.

reviews.author: DBC
reviews.text: Woodstock is one of the greatest spectacles and social experiments ever caught on film. Several hundred thousand people overtook a small sleepy farm (then town) in upstate New York for a weekend in August, catching most everyone off guard by the size of the turnout. Then all those people came together, tuned in with each other (thanks, acid), and held an event that really was about 3 days of peace, love, fun, and music.

reviews.author: Paul Elliott
reviews.text: Michael Wadleigh’s documentary film chronicles the titular three-day rock concert and pivotal moment of sixties counterculture quite brilliantly. reviews.author: ro2_rock
reviews.text: Wrinkles (Arrugas) is yet another shining example of why GKIDS Films has one of the most impressive animation catalogs out there. This film delivers a heartbreaking yet deeply satisfying story, tackling themes of aging, memory loss, and the fear of being forgotten with a level of sensitivity and emotional depth that few animated films achieve. What makes Wrinkles so special is how seamlessly these heavier themes blend with friendship and dignity in old age, creating a tone that is both melancholic and uplifting at the same time.

Emilio y Miguel son de los camaradas cinematográficos que siempre recordaré con nostalgia. Tiene escenas muy lindas y hay un flashback en donde cuentan la historia de una nube que es de las cosas más bonitas que veré este año.

Falo de soluços de homem, uma coisa bastante rara. O filme se chamava The Prowler. Eu não podia falar dele, pois as palavras o trairiam, como trairiam The Big Night. O que eu sei é que ele não esquematizava, como Lang; não se dispersava, como Preminger; não se deixava corromper, como Fuller. O que ele mostrava, e sua franqueza, sua honestidade desconcertava como um soco, era um ser maior que os heróis, mais belo que os deuses; era um homem. O cinema é a arte do verdadeiro; Joseph Losey é o primeiro artista. (Jacques Serguine, "Educação do Espectador [ou a escola do Mac-Mahon]")

Instead, it is a gangster film with a light dose of the former two qualities, both of which are drowned out in hyper-macho posturing, actual racism, and sexism. reviews.author: Arthur Tuoto

A repórter tem um papel ativo tanto no acontecimento que parte de uma relação perversa entre imagem pública e bem-estar social, quanto na esfera pessoal do protagonista. Como se toda energia fosse uma só, e nesse sentido a atenção que Cimino dá as cenas dos casais é reveladora. Os problemas de um ambiente coletivo que dependem diretamente da disposição para governar a própria individualidade.

reviews.text: "This would probably be Klaus Nomi's favorite movie if he ever got to watch it", I jokingly said during the wonderful opening act of the film, and returned to the thought with a reassured security after the finale. It really could be, with the film's new wave cabaret sensibility giving way to musical numbers romanticizing bestiality, ventriloquists rambling about foreign politics, and Jourdan and Kinski philosophizing about humanity's undeniable ties to the animal kingdom despite its insistance on distancing itself from it. La Belle et la Bête inside the heart struggling between the former's complience to rationality or succumbing to the latter's sensual, violent nature; the failed attempt at making those animalistic impulses belong to human law, for the law is disorder, especially after civilized society has been rendered obsolete. "Are we not men?", no! Let the beast loose!

reviews.author: Jack🧠
reviews.text: A glacial chamber opera staged in a cobalt-blue vacuum, Zoo zéro stands as a singular artefact of late 70s European avant-garde cinema. It is clinical, largely affectless, and meticulously abstract. Fleischer constructs a sealed system governed by repetition, mirrored gestures, and philosophical non sequiturs, where narrative dissolves into spatial arrangement. Catherine Jourdan and Klaus Kinski move as if under observation, stripped of interiority, delivering language emptied of consequence. The film abandons conventional storytelling in favour of pure mechanism, a controlled environment of ruptured continuity and suspended meaning. It functions as an artistic experiment rather than a scientific one, privileging aesthetic exploration over empirical logic. What emerges is a cabaret of entropy, preserved in formaldehyde, mutely staging its own collapse.
